rfi.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a combative defence of Washington’s right to wield its “national power” in Athens on Wednesday, while urging Europe to “awaken from its long slumber”.

rfi.title: ‘I became their slave’: Israeli hostage recounts 500 days in Hamas captivity
rfi.description: Omer Shem Tov was abducted by Hamas at the Nova music festival in Israel on 7 October, 2023 and held hostage by the armed Islamist group for 505 days. The 24-year-old has published a book about his time in captivity, entitled Meeting Myself in Hell. RFI spoke to him at his parents' home near Tel Aviv.

rfi.title: Three years on from the 7 October attacks, war has redrawn the map of Palestine
rfi.description: More than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed in the war launched by Israel following the 7 October, 2023 Hamas attacks. Palestinian territory has also become increasingly fragmented – in Gaza, the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem.

rfi.title: Franco-Japanese duo Kagan and Soai win 2026 Nobel Prize in chemistry
rfi.description: The Nobel Prize in chemistry was awarded on Wednesday to French scientist Henri B. Kagan and Japan’s Kenso Soai for unravelling the mystery of why only one of two forms of certain molecules occurs in nature.

rfi.title: France's Prime Minister Lecornu to address the nation over student protests
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will address the nation on Wednesday evening as part of his government's drive to end the wave of student blockades, which have closed high schools throughout the country.

rfi.title: African Union to launch continent's first credit rating agency in Mauritius
rfi.description: The African Union is launching the continent’s first credit rating agency on Wednesday, aiming to provide an alternative to the global “big three” by drawing on African expertise and perspectives.

rfi.title: Malian army retakes strategic city of Kidal after Tuareg separatists withdraw
rfi.description: The Malian army and its Russian allies entered the strategic northern city of Kidal on Tuesday without resistance after Tuareg separatists announced a tactical withdrawal, five months after government forces were driven out.

rfi.title: France earmarks a further €7m to help fight DRC's worst-ever Ebola crisis
rfi.description: France has decided to allocate an additional €7 million this year to combat the Ebola epidemic currently ravaging the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This comes as Kenya announced its first-ever death from the disease.

rfi.title: EU suspends beef exports from Namibia due to foot and mouth disease
rfi.description: The largest market for Namibian beef, the European Union, announced it has suspended imports after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, which wreaked havoc in Europe 25 years ago.

rfi.title: French MEP Hassan under investigation over flag incident at 7 October commemoration
rfi.description: Hard-left French EU lawmaker Rima Hassan is facing an investigation after the Israeli and European Union flags were allegedly thrown to the floor at a commemoration for the 2023 Hamas attacks that set off the Gaza war. Hassan said the action was to denounce the "ongoing genocide by the Israeli government".

rfi.title: Quebec separatist party wins provincial election in test of Canada's unity
rfi.description: Separatists won provincial elections in Quebec on Monday, with a promise to hold a vote on leaving Canada after US President Donald Trump leaves office, testing Prime Minister Mark Carney's message of national unity.

rfi.title: Argentina boss Scaloni salutes 'inimitable' Messi after maestro's final game
rfi.description: Argentina’s head coach Lionel Scaloni hailed the enduring genius of the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain striker Lionel Messi on Wednesday moments after the 39-year-old played his last game for the national team.

rfi.title: French PM slams violence at student protests and promises 'timeout' for democracy
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said there can be "no room for tolerance of violence", as tens of thousands of students took to the streets nationwide on Tuesday to protest over the state of schools. He told parliament that high schools would clear their schedules for the rest of the week to create space for democratic debate and air grievances.

rfi.title: Tens of thousands expected in Paris for high school protests
rfi.description: Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected on the streets of Paris on Tuesday as France's powerful trade unions join high school students rallying for better conditions in a wave of protests marked by clashes with police.

rfi.title: Olise strikes twice in France's romp past Belgium in Nations League
rfi.description: Désiré Doué, Ryan Cherki and two goals from Michael Olise launched the late pyrotechnics on Monday night at the Stade de France as France scored four times in 13 minutes to whoosh past Belgium 4-1 and maintain the lead of their Nations League pool.

rfi.title: Lebanon joined by UK and France for three weeks of joint military drills
rfi.description: Lebanon's army will hold three weeks of exercises with the British military from Tuesday, both sides said on Monday, with the drills to involve personnel and representatives from countries including France, Italy and the United States.

rfi.title: Climate change driving child marriages and teen pregnancies, study finds
rfi.description: The charity Plan International said on Monday that global warming has increased the risk of child marriages, teenage pregnancies and violence against girls. Its report coincides with talks in the South Pacific nations of Fiji and Tuvalu, where climate change is affecting all aspects of daily life.

rfi.title: Study shows extreme poverty and homelessness on the rise in France
rfi.description: An international study published on Monday by France’s largest food aid charity, Restos du Cœur, shows the number of people living in extreme poverty in France and other wealthy countries increased by 37 percent between 2018 and 2025.

euronews.description: Haruka Kaju extended her unbeaten World Judo Tour run to 40 contests, defending her -63kg world title against Kerem Primo. At -81kg, Tato Grigalashvili defeated home favourite Zelim Tckaev to claim his fourth world title and return to the top of the podium.

euronews.title: Southern right whales return to South Africa, drawing crowds to the coast
euronews.description: Southern right whales return to Hermanus, South Africa, drawing crowds to the cliffs and whale festival as mothers nurse newborn calves in Walker Bay.

euronews.title: Rubio in Athens urges Europe to shoulder more of its defence burden
euronews.description: The US secretary of state held talks on energy, military cooperation and regional security, pointing to Greece as an example of higher defence spending. The agenda also included LNG, F-35s, the Eastern Mediterranean and the Strait of Hormuz.

euronews.title: Knife attack at Polish school: in Ostroleka a student injures seven, two are in critical condition
euronews.description: On Wednesday morning at a vocational school in Ostrołęka in Northern Poland, a 19-year-old pupil attacked classmates and teachers with a sharp tool, injuring seven people, two of whom are in a serious condition, police said.

euronews.title: Fantasy worlds come to life on nails at London nail art competition

euronews.description: The European Union has a plan to safeguard the Black Sea. But days after drones wreaked havoc along Romania and Bulgaria’s coast, sinking commercial vessels and killing two people, questions loom over how Brussels can protect the sea.

euronews.title: Residents search belongings after Jerusalem building demolished
euronews.description: A five-storey building in Jerusalem’s al-Tur was demolished by Israeli authorities over alleged lack of permits, displacing dozens of Palestinian residents.

Dans les faits, par le biais d’une société-écran, Moscou en organise la confiscation. Après la mise « sous administration temporaire » devrait venir la répartition de ces actifs entre sociétés amies.

lemonde.title: « On est encore au Moyen Age » : dans l’e-sport, les femmes en première ligne des violences sexistes et sexuelles
lemonde.description: Un streameur et commentateur réputé de « League of Legends » a été mis en examen en juillet pour viol, selon les informations du « Monde ». Un cas révélateur des violences sexuelles qui n’épargnent pas l’e-sport, un secteur très masculin au sein duquel la parole des femmes peine à être écoutée.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, le réveil d’une gauche socialiste et démocrate, portée par une nouvelle génération d’élus et de militants

Les candidats de cette mouvance, trentenaires ou quadragénaires, espèrent remporter des victoires décisives aux midterms du 3 novembre.

lemonde.title: Un traitement optogénétique redonne une vision partielle à six patients aveugles

lemonde.title: Christa Pike, qui a survécu à son exécution aux Etats-Unis, a repris connaissance et se dit « en colère et désorientée »

lemonde.title: Crise du logement en Espagne : l’octogénaire expulsée à l’origine du mouvement de protestation est morte
lemonde.description: Maricarmen Abascal, 87 ans, avait été hospitalisée dans un état d’épuisement après son expulsion, bien qu’un accord ait été obtenu avec la société propriétaire pour qu’elle puisse réintégrer son appartement.

lemonde.description: Le Rassemblement national a présenté un contre-budget pour 2027 et une trajectoire financière pour le prochain quinquennat. Marine Le Pen, en cas de victoire à la présidentielle, attend un effort de 8,2 milliards d’euros des collectivités locales dès l’an prochain.

lemonde.title: Les élus de Paris veulent réduire l’étendue de la zone soumise à la protection du patrimoine dans la capitale
lemonde.description: La majorité municipale de gauche entend réétudier le périmètre du site patrimonial remarquable, qu’elle juge trop vaste : il comporte actuellement les sept premiers arrondissements de la capitale, ainsi qu’une partie de quatre autres arrondissements.

lemonde.title: L’ouverture d’une base chinoise au Laos, après l’installation d’une autre au Cambodge, inquiète les pays de la région
lemonde.description: Avec la création d’un centre de formation de pilotes sur la base rénovée de Ban Keun, le Laos devient le second pays d’Asie du Sud-Est, après le Cambodge, à accueillir une infrastructure d’entraînement militaire conjointe avec la Chine.

lemonde.title: Le Français Henri Kagan, un Nobel de chimie très attendu
lemonde.description: Le chercheur a été récompensé, mercredi, avec le Japonais Kenso Soai. Ils ont été mis à l’honneur pour leurs travaux sur la catalyse asymétrique.

lemonde.title: Entre les Etats-Unis et la Grèce, une alliance et une coopération énergétique sans précédent
lemonde.description: En visite à Athènes, le secrétaire d’Etat américain, Marco Rubio, a appelé l’Europe à sortir de « sa torpeur » et a au contraire salué le rôle de la Grèce, « l’alliée [de Washington] face à la question migratoire et aux menaces terroristes ».

lemonde.title: Les affections longue durée ont coûté près de 20 milliards d’euros à l’Assurance-maladie en 2025
lemonde.description: En dix ans, les dépenses de l’Assurance-maladie liées aux affections longue durée ont augmenté de 8,2 milliards d’euros (+ 72 % en euros courants). Et ce, en raison du vieillissement de la population, d’une hausse de la prévalence des maladies chroniques et du coût des traitements.

france24fr.title: Espagne : Maricarmen, la retraitée devenue symbole de la crise du logement, est morte
france24fr.description: Maricarmen, une femme de 87 ans, avait été expulsée de son appartement à Madrid le 23 septembre. Dans la foulée, des milliers de personnes étaient descendues dans la rue pour manifester contre la crise du logement en Espagne. La retraitée est morte mercredi, a annoncé un syndicat de locataires.

france24fr.title: Mali : après Kidal, quelles perspectives pour l'armée dans le nord ?
france24fr.description: 🇲🇱 La reprise de Kidal marque un tournant pour l’armée malienne, après sept mois de revers. Les FAMA ont repris cette ville stratégique sans combat, à la suite du repli des Touaregs du FLA. Reste désormais à consolider ce succès dans le Nord.

france24fr.title: 7-Octobre : quel avenir pour Israël ?
france24fr.description: Trois ans après l’attaque du 7 octobre 2023 en Israël, la plus meurtrière jamais perpétrée dans le pays par le Hamas, des commémorations se sont tenues tout au long de la journée. Cette attaque avait déclenché une vaste offensive israélienne dans la bande de Gaza. Cet anniversaire intervient cette année dans un contexte politique particulièrement tendu, à l’approche des élections législatives.

france24fr.title: Lecornu joue l'apaisement avec les lycéens et annonce des mesures sur le prix de l'essence

france24fr.title: L'Australie, future présidente de la COP, pourtant toujours très dépendante du charbon

france24fr.title: Aux Comores, une nouvelle loi inquiète la communauté malgache
france24fr.description: Aux Comores, une nouvelle loi, votée mais pas encore appliquée, réserve certaines activités de petit commerce aux seuls Comoriens de naissance. Une mesure qui inquiète vivement la communauté malgache installée dans l'archipel. Récit de Maya-Anaïs Yataghène.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : la France offre des drones à l'armée malgache
france24fr.description: Catherine Vautrin, ministre française des Armées, était ce mardi à Madagascar pour une visite de quelques heures. france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : le redécoupage électoral peut-il faire basculer le Congrès ?
france24fr.description: À l’approche des élections de mi-mandat, les redécoupages électoraux sont au cœur de la bataille entre républicains et démocrates. france24fr.title: Ukraine : une frappe russe sur un immeuble fait 18 morts à Prylouky
france24fr.description: De nouvelles frappes de missiles russes touchent l’Ukraine : à Prylouky, un immeuble a été frappé, faisant 18 morts. Une nouvelle attaque meurtrière contre une zone résidentielle, racontée par Ludovic de Foucaud.

france24fr.title: Midterms : les démocrates peuvent-ils reprendre le Congrès à Trump ?
france24fr.description: Donald Trump parviendra-t-il à préserver la majorité républicaine au Congrès lors des élections de mi-mandat ? Hausse des prix, immigration, intelligence artificielle et guerre en Iran : sa politique intérieure et étrangère s’invite dans la campagne, tandis que les démocrates cherchent à reconquérir les sièges décisifs. spiegel.description: Im besetzten Westjordanland ist ein 44-jähriger Palästinenser bei einem Angriff israelischer Siedler getötet worden. Siedler-Gewalt erschwert palästinensischen Bauern zunehmend den Zugang zu ihren Olivenhainen.

spiegel.title: John Coale: Dreht Donald Trumps Ex-Anwalt jetzt die US-Strategie für Russland?
spiegel.description: John Coale soll offenbar die festgefahrenen Gespräche mit dem Kreml voranbringen. Einem Medienbericht zufolge mit einem Wirtschaftsdeal nach belarussischem Vorbild. Gegen den Willen der Ukraine.

spiegel.title: Saudi-Arabien: Huthi-Miliz bekennt sich zu Angriffen auf Flughäfen in Riad und Abha
spiegel.description: Bei Raketentreffern sind auf zwei Flughäfen in Saudi-Arabien drei Menschen getötet und Dutzende weitere verletzt worden. Die Huthi-Miliz erklärte, sie habe die Attacken ausgeführt.

spiegel.title: Minnesota: FBI vereitelt mutmaßlichen Terroranschlag auf Einkaufszentrum
spiegel.description: Ein 18-Jähriger soll einen Terroranschlag im US-Bundesstaat Minnesota geplant haben. Das FBI nahm den Mann fest, nachdem er von einem verdeckten Ermittler ein Sturmgewehr gekauft hatte. Er wollte wohl bis zu 60 Menschen töten.

spiegel.title: Christa Pike: Anwälte schildern Gesundheitszustand nach gescheiterter Hinrichtung
spiegel.description: Christa Pike leidet nach der missglückten Hinrichtung an einer Lungenentzündung und kann weder essen noch ihre Arme bewegen, so ihr Anwalt. Dieser fordert Zugang zu den Beweismitteln.

spiegel.title: Maricarmen: Spanierin, deren Wohnung zwangsgeräumt wurde, ist tot
spiegel.description: María del Carmen Abascal, die ihre Wohnung zwangsweise verlassen musste, ist im Alter von 87 Jahren gestorben. Ihr Fall hatte in Spanien Proteste gegen die Wohnungskrise ausgelöst.

spiegel.title: Salt and Silver: Warum sich die Gründer Riffelmacher und Kosikowski trennen
spiegel.description: Zwei Köche, eine Symbiose: Der Aufstieg der Salt-&-Silver-Gründer Johannes Riffelmacher und Thomas Kosikowski wirkte wie eine Party. Nun trennen sie sich, sprechen erstmals über Kosikowskis Alkoholsucht – und unüberwindbare Differenzen.

spiegel.title: Haustiere: Mit Hunden das Bett zu teilen, macht Schlaf nicht schlechter
spiegel.description: Mal wieder hundemüde? Viele Frauchen und Herrchen schlafen mit ihrem Haustier im Bett, auch wenn sie morgens das Gefühl haben, dadurch oft wach geworden zu sein. Forschende haben das überprüft.

spiegel.title: New York: Tishman Speyer investiert in Chrysler-Gebäude
spiegel.description: Auch wegen des Denkmalschutzes gestaltete sich die Suche nach einem Käufer langwierig. Nun will das Immobilienunternehmen Tishman Speyer 235 Millionen US-Dollar in den Wolkenkratzer investieren.

spiegel.title: Berlin Abgeordnetenhauswahl 2026: Müssten AfD und Linke je ein Mandat verlieren?
spiegel.description: Berlin hat gewählt – doch möglicherweise müssen AfD und Linke zwei sicher geglaubte Sitze im Abgeordnetenhaus wieder abgeben. Grund für die Verwirrung: ein schlampig reformiertes Gesetz.

spiegel.title: Sachsen: Sexistische Diskriminierung – Studie deckt Defizite bei Polizei auf
spiegel.description: Griffe unter den Rock, sexistische Sprüche, unerwünschte Kontakte: Eine Studie der Uni Leipzig beschreibt vielfältige Formen von Sexismus bei der sächsischen Polizei. Auch beim Umgang mit Fehlverhalten sehen die Forschenden Defizite.

spiegel.title: Antisemitismus in Deutschland: Zwei Juden streiten über Gefahr von links und rechts
spiegel.description: Ist die Wahl der Linken in Berlin ein »Super-GAU« – oder kommt die wahre Gefahr von rechts? Milena Glimbovski und Ben Salomo, beide Juden aus der Hauptstadt, teilen die Sorge vor mehr Antisemitismus, blicken aber unterschiedlich auf die Partei.

spiegel.title: WHO verlangt Informationen von Russland über mögliche Pest-Infektion
spiegel.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation will mehr über den Tod einer Mitarbeiterin eines russischen Instituts für Seuchenbekämpfung erfahren. Außerdem soll der Kreml Stellung zu Gerüchten über einen angeblichen zweiten Vorfall nehmen.

spiegel.title: Die Grünen: Jugendorganisation wirft Franziska Brantner Anbiederung an CDU vor
spiegel.description: Nach der Wahl des AfD-Landtagspräsidenten in Sachsen-Anhalt streiten auch die Grünen. Henriette Held, Bundessprecherin der Jugendorganisation, vermisst bei Parteichefin Brantner klare Kritik an der CDU.

spiegel.title: Emden wird Marinestützpunkt: »Wir sind eine sehr verunsicherte Stadtgesellschaft zur Zeit«
spiegel.description: Auf einem kargen Landstrich nahe der Emder Innenstadt soll ein Marinehafen entstehen, mehr als doppelt so groß wie das Fürstentum Monaco. Das bringt Arbeitsplätze. Aber auch die Gefahr, Ziel eines Angriffs zu werden.

spiegel.title: Digitale Gewalt: »Für uns ist das Wichtigste, dass die Taten bestraft werden«
spiegel.description: Sexualisierte Deepfakes und voyeuristische Aufnahmen sollen künftig strafbar sein. Einen entsprechenden Gesetzentwurf hat das Kabinett beschlossen. Was Betroffene und Prominente dazu sagen.

spiegel.title: Go Asia: Als giftig eingestufter Farn wird zurückgerufen
spiegel.description: In zwölf Bundesländern waren sie zu kaufen: 280-Gramm-Gläser mit Farn, das in der EU nicht zugelassen ist. Die Produkte können in Filialen von Go Asia zurückgegeben werden.

observador.title: Spotify expande oferta de audiolivros a mais de 180 mercados
observador.description: Mais de 350 mil títulos em 120 línguas, incluindo português. Os ouvintes mensais cresceram quase 40% num ano e as horas escutadas mais de 30%.

observador.title: Maduro e Flores podem enfrentar acusações de tortura
observador.description: Maduro e Flores podem ser acusado de tortura contra mais de uma dezena de norte-americanos detidos ilegalmente na Venezuela. Advogado de Maduro afirma não ter recebido nenhuma notificação.

observador.title: Rosa Sousa candidata dos TSD à presidência da UGT
observador.description: A presidente do Sindicato dos Quadros Técnicos do Estado foi escolhida por "plena concordância" para disputar a presidência da central sindical no congresso deste fim de semana.

observador.title: STF não solta Bolsonaro antes da segunda volta
observador.description: Kassio Nunes Marques, relator do processo de revisão criminal do ex-presidente preso por golpe de Estado, quer evitar interferência no acto eleitoral de 25 de outubro.

observador.title: Jovem acusado de planear atentado em centro comercial
observador.description: Autoridades tentaram avisar pais do rapaz, que quereria cometer atentado como apoio ao estado Islâmico. Tinha uma espingarda e centenas de munições.

observador.title: Condenado a quase seis anos por tentar matar militar da GNR
observador.description: A arma estava escondida numa bolsa e modificada para ser portátil. O militar só escapou porque deu o alerta e os três guardas no local conseguiram desviar a espingarda e manietá-lo.

observador.title: Oposição russa assinala 20 anos da morte de Politkovskaya
observador.description: Homenagem foi acompanhada pela polícia, que chegou a abordar uma pessoa que colocou flores junto ao memorial. Jornalista investigou crimes de guerra na Chechénia e a corrupção no círculo de Putin.

observador.title: Quinta dos Ingleses. Câmara pode avançar contra opositores
observador.description: Após decisão de providência cautelar, autarca de Cascais prepara processo para ressarcir o município. Ambientalistas alertam: declarações já foram comunicadas à magistrada do caso.

observador.title: Ex-diretor do SIRESP: falhas do apagão não se repetiriam
observador.description: Substituição de baterias feita após o apagão de abril de 2025 — quando 25 a 30% das estações falharam — garante agora maior resiliência do sistema de emergência.

observador.title: Vice-campeã europeia Camila Rebelo reforça Benfica
observador.description: Olímpica em Paris 2024 e vice-campeã europeia dos 200 costas, a nadadora junta-se a Diogo Ribeiro e Diana Durães no clube lisboeta.

observador.title: ADI garante maioria com acordo parlamentar
observador.description: O partido que ficou em segundo nas legislativas de 27 de setembro fica no poder. A coligação MCI-PS/PUN dá os seis mandatos que faltavam para os 29 votos na Assembleia Nacional.

observador.title: Petroleiro atingido perto do Qatar no estreito de Ormuz
observador.description: O ataque ocorreu a 94 km da costa do Qatar. Rubio, em Atenas, diz que o fluxo de petróleo voltou aos níveis pré-guerra e que a economia iraniana será "catastrófica".

observador.title: 22h. Governo entrega amanhã proposta de Orçamento do Estado
observador.description: Ministro das Finanças vai entregar documento por volta das duas horas da tarde no Parlamento. Ainda, líder do PS diz que não espera surpresas no Orçamento para 2027 e volta a confirmar viabilização.

observador.title: Seguro recebe governador do Banco de Portugal em Belém
observador.description: A reunião em Belém, com Álvaro Santos Pereira, coincidiu com a publicação do Boletim Económico de outubro e antecede a entrega do OE2027 à Assembleia.

observador.title: EUA banem marcas com 15% nas mãos de chineses. Não Mercedes
observador.description: Os EUA defendem as suas marcas, propondo banir construtores em que os chineses detêm mais de 15%. A Mercedes ultrapassa esse limite, mas não vai ser impedida de disputar o mercado.

observador.title: O filme do ataque com cocktail molotov em frente à AR
observador.description: Relação refez passos de Nelson Vassalo, que atacou "Marcha pela Vida" com cocktail molotov, e concluiu que arguido pegou fogo ao rastilho do engenho — que, por sorte, não incendiou mulheres e crianças

observador.title: Ventura: "Acordos escondidos são com o PS e PSD"
observador.description: André Ventura garantiu que o entendimento com o Governo foi "escrito e tornado público" e desafiou Carneiro a explicar por que vota um OE que ainda não conhece.

observador.title: Livre questiona erro da CGA em 3.000 pensões
observador.description: Partido quer saber o fundamento legal para reduzir pensões já comunicadas como definitivas. Ministra confirmou erro e disse que valores pagos a mais terão de ser devolvidos.

elpais.title: Muere Maricarmen, la mujer que encendió la lucha contra los desahucios en España
elpais.description: La mujer de 87 años ha fallecido este miércoles en el Hospital Gregorio Marañón de Madrid, según ha confirmado el Sindicato de Inquilinas en un comunicado

elpais.title: Última hora tras la muerte de Maricarmen, en directo|Feijóo pide que no se haga una “utilización interesada” de la muerte de Maricarmen
elpais.description: La abogada de Maricarmen: “Si se hubiera suspendido el desahucio, hoy no estaríamos en esta situación” | El PP veta un minuto de silencio por Maricarmen en la Asamblea de Madrid | Al menos un millar de personas marchan hasta el Congreso y encienden velas en su memoria al grito de “asesinos”

elpais.title: Maricarmen cambió España
elpais.description: El legado de la mujer desahuciada en Madrid interpela a toda la sociedad

elpais.title: Maricarmen murió horas antes de firmar su contrato de alquiler para ocho años y recuperar su casa
elpais.description: El estado de la mujer, de 87 años, se agravó inesperadamente en la mañana del miércoles y falleció en el hospital Gregorio Marañón a las 19.30 acompañada de familiares y seres queridos más cercanos

elpais.title: Cronología del caso Maricarmen: de cuatro intentos de desahucio a un movimiento nacional por la vivienda
elpais.description: La mujer de 87 años fue desalojada hace dos semanas y ha fallecido este miércoles en el hospital Gregorio Marañón

elpais.title: Las imágenes de la vida de Maricarmen y su lucha por evitar los desahucios
elpais.description: La mujer de 87 años que fue desahuciada de su piso el pasado 23 de septiembre, ha fallecido el en Hopital Gregorio Marañon donde permanecía ingresada desde entonces

elpais.title: “Maricarmen tiene que ser la última víctima del sistema”: cientos de acampados marchan desde Sol al Congreso
elpais.description: La muerte de la vecina madrileña sacude la acampada de Sol, que responde con una protesta hasta la Cámara baja entre gritos de “asesinos”

elpais.title: Los líderes políticos reaccionan al fallecimiento del símbolo de los desahuciados: “La muerte de Maricarmen nos golpea”
elpais.description: Las cuentas en redes sociales de varios representantes de partidos difunden mensajes de pésame y llamadas a evitar más casos como el de la octogenaria madrileña

elpais.title: El Sindicato de Inquilinas llama a la huelga general por la vivienda “para que no haya una Maricarmen más”
elpais.description: El sindicato confirma el paro el 11 de noviembre junto a CGT, CO.BAS y Solidaridad Obrera. CC OO y UGT piden en un comunicado movilización de los trabajadores “por una vivienda digna”

elpais.title: La lucha de Maricarmen, en imágenes
elpais.description: La mujer, que impulsó la lucha contra los desahucios en España, ha fallecido este miércoles a los 87 años en Madrid

elpais.title: Dejad a la gente morir en sus pisos
elpais.description: En España no se puede empezar a vivir porque no tienes casa, ni se puede empezar a morir porque te echan de ella

elpais.title: Maricarmen; su muerte no será en vano
elpais.description: Esta muerte debiera señalar a todos aquellos que no tuvieron la más mínima piedad en una anciana que salió de su casa con los ojos asustados

elpais.title: Maricarmen, santa súbita
elpais.description: Sufrió el martirio de quienes la lapidaron buscando pecados que arrojarle a la cara para arrastrarla por el fango estando ya en la cama hospitalaria que iba a ser su lecho de muerte

elpais.title: Maricarmen, la bola negra de España
elpais.description: Nada va a ser igual en el romance sonámbulo de esta sociedad adormecida a la que han ido linchando a base de alquileres, hipotecas y desahucios sin lógica ni ética

elpais.title: Más Madrid propone que Colau sea la candidata del Frente Amplio a la presidencia del Gobierno y encabece la lista en Barcelona
elpais.description: Mónica García liderará la papeleta en Madrid junto a Emilio Delgado, Tesh Sidi y Eduardo Rubiño, según trasladan fuentes del partido. Comuns admite “avances” pero evita dar por cerrada la negociación

elpais.title: Felipe González critica al Gobierno por cuestionar al Congreso y al PP por dudar del voto por correo
elpais.description: El expresidente expresa su desencanto con Sánchez y Feijóo en el homenaje a Fernández Vara y a Lambán, fallecidos hace un año

elpais.title: Feijóo abona las dudas del PP sobre el voto por correo y pedirá “medidas adicionales” a la Junta Electoral
elpais.description: El líder del PP arranca la precampaña en Ceuta, donde afirma que habría utilizado a las fuerzas de seguridad el día de la entrada masiva

elpais.title: ¿Cómo se mueven los votos desde 2023? Las encuestas por sexo, renta, edad e ideología
elpais.description: Vox crece en general y especialmente en un grupo: mujeres jóvenes. El PP tiene fugas por la derecha y el PSOE sobre todo por el centro

republika.title: A Padova il ‘tribunale islamico’: “Giudicheremo con la Sharia”. Insorgono Lega e Fn
republika.description: La camera arbitraria islamica è nata il 3 marzo e serve a “risolvere controversie civili e commerciali in conformità con i principi della Sharia”

republika.title: “Io, autore del falso Eco: ecco perché l’ho fatto. Insegno, creare fake coi ragazzi li aiuta”
republika.description: La “bustina di Minerva” attribuita al celebre prof che insegnava a Bologna, apparsa in rete il primo ottobre e diventata virale, è stata realizzata da Ciro Ascione in dialogo con ChatGpt. Lui è citato anche su Wikipedia: “Amo giocare sulla contaminazione”

republika.title: Spagna, è morta Maricarmen: simbolo della protesta per la casa
republika.description: Le condoglianze del premier Sánchez: “Sentiamo la sua perdita come nostra”. La donna, 87 anni, invalida, era stata sfrattata dalla sua abitazione a Madrid il 23 settembre. Per lei il Paese è sceso in piazza e le pressioni del movimento hanno attivato la crisi di governo

republika.title: Sospetto secondo caso di morte per peste polmonare in Russia, il Cremlino smentisce. Trump: “Non pensiamo sia un’arma biologica”
republika.description: Il presidente Usa: “A sentire loro la situazione è sotto controllo”. L’Oms chiede chiarimenti a Mosca: “La condivisione tempestiva, completa e trasparente delle informazioni, è fondamentale per chiarire notizie contrastanti”

republika.title: Stefania Corna, addio all’ex palleggiatrice di Scandicci e della nazionale: aveva 35 anni
republika.description: Ha vinto la Coppa Italia nel 2008

republika.title: Apocalisse nucleare, parte l’esercitazione Nato in Italia. La protesta di Avs
republika.description: Il 13 ottobre iniziano le simulazioni di “Steadfast Noon” nei nostri cieli, con simulacri delle bombe tattiche americane. L’interrogazione di Bonelli: “Nessuna comunicazione dal governo. Via le testate Usa dal nostro Paese”

republika.title: Mattarella concede tre grazie: c’è anche Guido Gianni, il gioielliere che uccise i due rapinatori
republika.description: Il catanese era stato condannato a dodici anni e quattro mesi. Salvini: “Sono felice. La difesa è sempre legittima”. Plauso anche da Forza Italia. La moglie: “Lui è il mio eroe”.Gli altri due casi legati a delitti in materia di stupefacenti

republika.title: Crans, Zurich dice no alla richiesta di Jessica Moretti di indennizzo per infortunio
republika.description: La compagnia assicurativa ritiene infondata la richiesta fatta per il “trauma psichico”. Il padre di Manfredi Marcucci: “I Moretti sono senza vergogna”

republika.title: Sinner ha provato ad anticipare il ritorno in campo: ecco cosa è successo
republika.description: Jannik ha accelerato il recupero e intensificato il ritmo degli allenamenti

republika.title: Garlasco, Dna maschile sulla bici di Stasi “dimenticato” in un armadio dei Ris
republika.description: Dopo la scoperta avvenuta solo nelle scorse settimane della mancanza del sangue di Chiara Poggi sui pedali, un nuovo mistero: un profilo mai indagato e né attribuito al suo proprietario

republika.title: MotoGp, dal 2027 nuovo format: la Sprint avrà la sua qualifica. Tutte le novità
republika.description: Introdotte una serie di modifiche, cambiano anche le qualifiche per la gara

republika.title: Weinstein accuses journalist Vicedomini of lying as Rome opens investigation
republika.description: The former producer claims the man who testified at his rape trial had been in a relationship with model Evgeniya Chernyshova

republika.title: Camion e bus, Salvini: “Al lavoro fino a 70 ma controlli serrati su autisti”. No della Cgil
republika.description: Il ministro dei Trasporti annuncia una misura volontaria per consentire ai conducenti di merci e passeggeri di restare in servizio più a lungo. Il sindacato si oppone: lavoro usurante, le persone devono uscire prima e non dopo

republika.title: Michael Douglas, le memorie del “bad guy” tra amori e eccessi: “Per molti è solo gossip”
republika.description: L’attore, 82 anni, racconta vita e carriera nell’autobiografia “One Helluva Ride” tra relazioni segrete sul set, abusi di alcol e cocaina

republika.title: Eni, il prezzo del diesel scende a 2,21. Meloni: “Spero ritorni price cap”
republika.description: Il prezzo del gasolio consigliato ai distributori torna a scendere in scia al calo delle quotazioni dei prodotti raffinati. La presidente del Consiglio: “Pronti a intervenire con accise mobili”

republika.title: Pa, firmato il contratto di medici e dirigenti della sanità. Aumenti lordi fino a 560 euro al mese
republika.description: Il rinnovo concluso oggi all’Aran vale per il triennio 2025-2027. Arretrati tra i 4.000 e i 6.000 euro

republika.title: Grave l’attore Davide Iacopini, aggredito mentre era in monopattino. Caccia alla banda della minicar
republika.description: Il volto di Suburra e Diaz il 5 ottobre è stato disarcionato con un calcio e ha battuto la testa: è ricoverato in terapia intensiva. Si indaga su altri casi avvenuti a Roma nel quartiere di Monteverde

republika.title: È morta Barbara Spinelli, giornalista ed europarlamentare. Fu tra i fondatori di Repubblica
republika.description: Figlia di Altiero Spinelli, padre ispiratore dell’Unione europea, aveva ottant’anni. Una carriera brillante come cronista ed editorialista, poi il passaggio in politica

nyt.title: From Iran to the U.K., Trump Is Being Forced Into Retreat
nyt.description: A war that was intended to demonstrate the reach of American power has now done the opposite. It is a lesson in unintended consequences.

nyt.title: Rubio Urges Europe to Awaken From ‘Slumber’ and Uphold Western Dominance
nyt.description: In Greece, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Western nations must embrace an earlier ethos of exploration and conquest as part of their civilization, to remain ‘at the head of the world.’

nyt.title: Christa Pike, Awake and Angry, Is at the Center of a Legal Storm
nyt.description: Her awareness and condition deepen ethical and legal questions after Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute her for murdering a classmate decades ago.

nyt.title: Texas Plans Execution After Botched Lethal Injection in Tennessee
nyt.description: Jamaal Howard’s lawyers are seeking information about the lethal injection drug, the same medication used in Tennessee’s failed attempt last week.

nyt.title: Mamdani Draws Anger With Oct. 7 Statement Denouncing Israel’s Gaza Attacks
nyt.description: After calling the anniversary of the attacks on Israel “profoundly painful,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani denounced Israel’s military action in Gaza, prompting criticism from some Jewish leaders.

nyt.title: If the Kennedy Center Is ‘Dangerous,’ Why Is the Symphony Rehearsing There?
nyt.description: The National Symphony Orchestra is practicing inside a building that President Trump and his allies say could fall on their heads.

nyt.title: Trump Administration Investigates Wells Fargo for Race-Based Lending
nyt.description: The federal housing agency says the bank’s efforts to encourage Black homeownership amount to discrimination.

nyt.title: Jonathan the Giant Tortoise Is 194 Years Old. He Just Had His Genome Sequenced.
nyt.description: Scientists have sequenced his genome for the first time, hoping the world’s oldest land animal can offer clues into the genetics of longevity.

nyt.title: Russia Says It Found No ‘Emergency’ in Plague Lab
nyt.description: New information around the death of a lab worker, including a statement that she had been vaccinated against the plague, came as U.S. officials demanded more data.

nyt.title: Fears of a Plague Outbreak in Russia: What to Know
nyt.description: Russian authorities aren’t saying much about the death of a woman who worked in a lab studying plague. But experts say any risk of contagion would be limited.

nyt.title: Bondage Photos Weren’t Part of the Campaign Plan
nyt.description: But Chris Gallant, a Black Hawk pilot and Democrat who is running to represent Long Island in Congress, is making the most of life post-tabloid reveal.

nyt.title: August Lamm Was an Influencer. Now She Wants You to Ditch Your Smartphone.
nyt.description: August Lamm wants you to put down your smartphone and reclaim your life.

nyt.title: ‘Maricarmen,’ Whose Eviction Enraged Spaniards, Dies at 87
nyt.description: María del Carmen Abascal, aged and ailing, became a symbol of the country’s housing crisis when she was evicted two weeks ago, prompting mass protests and triggering national elections.

nyt.title: Pete Hegseth’s ‘Vast Overcorrection’
nyt.description: A Special Forces veteran joins the columnist David French to assess Pete Hegseth’s leadership.

nyt.title: ‘The Twilight Zone’ Created a Blueprint for Surviving Our Surreal Moment
nyt.description: With “The Twilight Zone,” Rod Serling created a durable blueprint for understanding our surreal reality.

nyt.title: Fatal Stabbing of a 7-Year-Old Girl Rattles Chicago: ‘That Was a Baby’
nyt.description: The attack has raised questions about whether the suspect was overlooked by authorities despite a history of mental health problems and violent offenses.

npr.title: What is the pneumonic plague?
npr.description: The ancient disease of plague is back in the headlines after the death this month of a Russian lab worker.

npr.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
npr.description: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

npr.title: Greetings from Lahore, Pakistan, whose high court offers an oasis for chatter and chai
npr.description: The Lahore High Court is a near-perfect specimen of British South Asian colonial architecture and its main square is a pleasant spot shaded by banyan trees.

npr.title: DIY fertilizer is a blessing as farmers face steep prices due to the Iran war
npr.description: It's hard enough being a small-scale farmer. Then the Iran war drove up fertilizer prices. So farmers are using a traditional Asian recipe to make their own. They call it a "labor of love."

npr.title: U.S. moves long-range bombers from U.K. And, Israel allegedly warned before Oct. 7
npr.description: A possible Iranian threat led the U.S. to remove long-range bombers from a U.K. base. And, Israelis are learning that their prime minister may have been warned before the Oct. 7 attacks.

npr.title: Investigation continues into whether U.K. air base incident is linked to Iran
npr.description: Questions continue to swirl around a U.K. military base and potential Iran-backed attacks.

npr.title: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai win Nobel Prize in chemistry
npr.description: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry Wednesday for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

npr.title: 3 years on, Israelis grapple with reports Netanyahu was warned before Oct. 7 attacks

phys-org.title: NYC congestion pricing policy linked to cleaner air in lower Manhattan
phys-org.description: One year after New York City launched its congestion pricing policy, fine particulate pollution inside Manhattan's congestion relief zone was 13% lower, according to a new analysis that accounted for regional pollution trends, weather and normal year-to-year variability.

phys-org.title: First-in-kind data set reveals insights across the world's national and regional economies
phys-org.description: The University of Virginia has published the Global Capitalism Index (GCI), a first-in-kind data set offering unprecedented insights into the globe's capitalism conditions in every country. Assembled from more than two hundred data sets across eight key pillars, the GCI's country-by-country scores offer an array of ways to understand capitalism around the world.

phys-org.title: Long Island measurements reveal household products and buildings as major summer pollution sources
phys-org.description: Products such as hairspray, paint and household disinfectants are increasingly causing summertime air pollution—and cities aren't accounting for it, which makes it harder to issue air quality advisories and enact regulations, new research from Colorado State University, the University of Minnesota and Purdue University shows.

phys-org.title: Hawaiian hot spot study uncovers evidence of true polar wander
phys-org.description: On Earth, everything is moving. The planet spins, the tectonic plates shift and the spin axis wobbles, as do the magnetic poles, which makes determining how things move a rather tricky proposition. For Rice University's Richard Gordon, this problem came up when he was trying to understand the history of the Hawaiian hot spot, the deep-mantle source of the volcanism that created the Hawaiian–Emperor chain of islands and underwater volcanoes.

phys-org.title: Eight-year analysis reveals how sunlight and nutrients shape sustainable urban farming
phys-org.description: Factors such as sunlight and stage-specific nutrient application determine crop success in urban agriculture, far beyond fixed recipes or miracle solutions. The findings are published in the journal Agronomy for Sustainable Development.

phys-org.title: 'Self-blinking dyes' simplify nanoscale imaging without sacrificing precision

When nanobodies are labeled with dyes, they can be used as probes to enhance super-resolution microscopy. However, conventional blinking dyes often perform poorly when attached to nanobodies, limiting their practical advantages. phys-org.title: Undergraduate student may have solved puzzle regarding isolated galaxies that have stopped producing stars
phys-org.description: An undergraduate astrophysics student at UC Berkeley has found three unusual galaxies—cataloged as Shapiro Dwarf Galaxies I, II and III. Each galaxy is far from other galaxies and has stopped making stars, a combination that is extremely rare. The discovery, published in The Astrophysical Journal, provides compelling observational evidence of a long-held astronomical theory.

phys-org.title: New approach to plant stress studies could yield hardier crops and medical insights
phys-org.description: At the University of Missouri, plant scientist Ron Mittler is rewriting the playbook for how scientists study life by asking what happens when living organisms face multiple stresses at once.

phys-org.title: New polystyrene uses 50% plant-based material and breaks into fragments for potential recycling
phys-org.description: Polystyrene is used in protective packaging for televisions and electronic devices, in decorative boards and baseboards for interior construction, and in petri dishes. It is one of the world's most important plastics, with nearly 20 million tons produced each year. The material is predominantly derived from crude oil and is rarely recycled. phys-org.description: A new type of advanced microscope (wide-field coherent multidimensional microscopy) has been developed. It uses a carefully designed sequence of ultrashort light pulses to study the behavior of high-tech materials, with potential practical applications in the study of innovative materials such as those used to build solar panels. phys-org.title: Ebola creates new hot spots in Congo as responders describe 'chaotic' response
phys-org.description: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is creating new hot spots where there's little to no support for patients, responders and officials say, as health workers admit there could still be a long way to go in fighting the disease that has killed over 4,000 people.

phys-org.title: First global genome atlas reveals overlooked microscopic life in hundreds of lakes and reservoirs
phys-org.description: Tiny single-celled organisms help keep lakes clear, but some can also contaminate the water. An international research team has analyzed DNA data from 362 lakes to create the first global genome atlas of these organisms. With the findings now published in Nature Communications, the new atlas lays the foundation for faster and more precise monitoring of lakes.

phys-org.title: Tiny plasma-grown particles enable easier magnetization reversal in materials for high-frequency electronics
phys-org.description: Researchers at South China University of Technology, in collaboration with the Dongguan Institute of Materials Science and Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, have developed a novel supranano multi-precipitate microstructure in amorphous soft magnetic composites using Ar/O₂ plasma treatment. By facilitating magnetic-moment reversal, this approach significantly reduced coercivity while maintaining excellent overall performance.

phys-org.title: Giant tortoises outnumber people in Seychelles, with nearly 183,000 on Aldabra
phys-org.description: A landmark survey of the world's largest free-roaming giant tortoise population has revealed that the once-endangered species is thriving and stable in the Seychelles.

phys-org.title: Vulnerability to heat waves varies greatly from one area to another within cities
phys-org.description: Extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and severe as a result of climate change. Heat waves are a prime example, as they have direct effects on health, thermal comfort and the livability of cities. That is why it is vital to conduct climate risk assessments to guide cities' adaptation policies and prioritize action in the most vulnerable areas.

phys-org.title: New display technology combines record brightness with pixels that stretch like rubber
phys-org.description: A research team led by Professor Jiwoong Yang of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering at DGIST has developed the world's first foundational technology for an ultrahigh-resolution stretchable quantum dot display (QLED) that can stretch freely like skin while maintaining sharp image quality. The findings were published in Nature Nanotechnology.

phys-org.title: Use of natural gas or propane in commercial kitchens exposes workers to air pollution and dangerous heat

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

proj-syn.title: How Africa Can Leverage the US-China Thaw
proj-syn.description: As dollar borrowing costs soar, Chinese rates are approaching record lows. This divergence, combined with the US-China thaw, creates an opportunity for African governments: partner with the US on gas and with China on solar and storage, and tap lower-cost Asian capital markets to finance investments in both.

proj-syn.title: Closing NATO’s Deterrence Gap
proj-syn.description: With Russian provocations against NATO member states growing more frequent, the alliance urgently needs to develop a credible doctrine of punitive deterrence to guide its response to acts of aggression that fall below the threshold of war. Mere territorial defense is not enough.

proj-syn.title: The India-Pakistan Cold War
proj-syn.description: The current stalemate between India and Pakistan should be viewed not as a pause between rounds of negotiation, but rather as part of a deliberate Indian strategy of disengagement. India will return to the negotiating table only after Pakistan dismantles, comprehensively and verifiably, its state-supported terrorist networks.

proj-syn.title: The Next Era of Reform Must Be About Capability
proj-syn.description: Economic development should no longer be measured solely by how much finance is mobilized or how much fiscal space is created. It must also be judged by whether countries emerge more capable of setting their own priorities, responding to challenges, and seizing new opportunities to shape their own future.

proj-syn.title: With AI, Sharing Is Caring
proj-syn.description: Although the public's distrust of Big Tech is understandable, given past experience, that is not a reason to starve AI models of the information and data they will need to be useful. If serving the public interest is the goal, everyone relying on the technology's output has a duty to provide high-quality input.

proj-syn.title: Why the US-China Trade Truce Matters
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump’s agreement to extend their trade truce reflects the fact that both sides have leverage over the other. In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, the current fragile equilibrium may be the best one can hope for.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Voters Have Moved
proj-syn.description: A strong performance by the right-wing, Donald Trump-aligned candidate in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election demonstrates that the left-wing ruling party has failed to keep up with the times. The Brazilian electorate is older, more devout, and more preoccupied with crime and personal security than it once was.

proj-syn.title: Does Inclusive Finance Really Need Stablecoins?
proj-syn.description: Today, 1.3 billion adults—more than half of them women—remain excluded from the formal financial system, and lower-income consumers still struggle to find and access the financial products and services they need. Contrary to much hype, stablecoins are not the best way to solve either of these problems.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Election Debacle Is Lula’s Fault
proj-syn.description: Brazil's left has just suffered a crushing election defeat and will most likely lose the presidency at the end of October. The causes are many, beginning with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's longstanding refusal to groom an appealing successor.

proj-syn.title: Sino-American Stability Without Trust
proj-syn.description: The main outcomes of the Trump-Xi summit—the two-month trade extension, the dialogue on AI, and even the carefully chosen language on Taiwan—point to Sino-American relations being in a holding pattern. For both sides, the main task is to prevent managed rivalry from devolving into outright confrontation.

proj-syn.title: Iran’s Moment of Opportunity
proj-syn.description: America and Israel's unilateral aggression against Iran lacked international legitimacy and predictably destabilized the entire region. But as justified as the Iranian leadership might feel in pursuing an obstinately maximalist strategy, it must be careful not to mistake short-term advantages for longer-term gains.

proj-syn.title: Is Russia’s Placement on the Security Council Legal?
proj-syn.description: When Russia replaced the Soviet Union as a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council in 1991, it did not even attempt to follow the process outlined in the UN Charter. Now that Russia’s usurpation of the USSR’s seat has enabled it to wage a war of aggression, the dubious legal status of its position must be revisited.

proj-syn.title: To Support Nepal, Waive Remittance Fees
proj-syn.description: To help Nepal move from rescue and relief toward reconstruction, money-transfer companies and banks ought to waive fees on remittances sent to the country for at least two months. Doing so could provide additional relief totaling several times more than what a recent emergency appeal by the United Nations generated.

proj-syn.title: What a Canada–Europe Alliance Needs
proj-syn.description: With trade, finance, technology, and supply chains having all become instruments of coercion, Canada, Europe, and other likeminded democracies must come together to defend their interests. But strategic convergence between governments is not enough; if a new alliance is to endure, it needs deep roots in society.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

proj-syn.title: Global AI Oversight Now
proj-syn.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

proj-syn.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
proj-syn.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

proj-syn.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
proj-syn.description: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.
